notes: WP3, multi-GPU without disproportionate overhead: the two ways llama.cpp lays one model
over several GCDs that work on ROCm, --split-mode layer (the default, every split measured
until now) and tensor (experimental tensor parallelism), on 2, 4 and 8 GCDs, against the
same model on one GCD (c01 dense-one-gcd, moe-one-gcd) and as replicas (c01 scale-replicas).
Layer split adds memory, not speed: four GCDs as layers wrote no faster than one
(12-09-2026, c01 scale-split, c02 split4 against split8). Tensor cuts each weight across
the GCDs and is what could make one request faster; batch 1 is the point of the campaign,
batch 16 says what it costs or gives with many requests.
Needs the engine of 15-10-2026 (next12): --split-mode. An architecture tensor parallelism
does not cover fails its load; that is a measurement, not a failure to retry.
Exclusive: the split's GCDs talk to each other over the node's links, which a neighbour
on the same links would share.
row was planned too and dropped on 15-10-2026: every load failed, as stock llama-bench's
does ("device ROCm0 does not support split buffers"): llama.cpp's CUDA/ROCm backend no
longer has them. The row points already queued for next12 fail in seconds.
rccl-* (added 15-10-2026, after r-split): tensor beat layer on 2 GCDs and collapsed on
4 and 8. ggml's all-reduce goes through NCCL/RCCL when compiled in, else its internal one,
which only exists for two devices, else a generic exchange; the engine had no RCCL. These
groups measure tensor again on a build with it (build_engine.sh EULLM_RCCL=1), and on 2
GCDs the internal all-reduce in the same binary (GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=internal) as control.
Labelled rccl in the spec, so only jobs submitted with EULLM_ENGINE_LABEL=rccl run them;
plan them alone: GROUP='rccl-*' ROUND=r-split-rccl EULLM_ENGINE_LABEL=rccl.
With RCCL (r-split-rccl, 16-10-2026) tensor no longer collapses beyond two GCDs: Qwen3-32B
on four writes 52.7 tokens/s to one request (layer 36.1) and 384 to 16 (layer 260); the
235B at 16 writes 110 on four and 107 on eight (layer 76.8, 75.7). rccl-batch, rccl-480b
and rccl-120b (added the same day) go on: 32 and 64 requests, the 480B on eight GCDs and
gpt-oss-120b on two and four, layer beside tensor in the same binary where c02 has no row.
Plan them alone: GROUP='rccl-batch rccl-480b rccl-120b' ROUND=r-split-rccl2.
